Topic: Modern Conservatism in the Global Midwest Description:This course examines the development of Modern Conservatism through global military conflicts, cultural transformations, electoral realignments, and economic shifts. In particular, we will explore the role and influence of conservative Midwesterners within the broader political movement from 1928 to the present in theGlobal Midwest. We will study issues that shaped and were shaped by conservatives including "right to work" campaigns, Vietnam War protests on college campuses, deindustrialization and globalization, the energy crisis of the 1970s, housing and school desegregation, busing, abortion, the sexual revolution, and the STOP-ERA campaign. Through these issues and events, we will reassess the impact and significance of Modern Conservatism on U.S. society through the 20th century.
